title: V-stitch
subtitle: Two trebles with a chain between them, worked into the same stitch
excerpt: The V-stitch places two trebles into the same base stitch with a single chain between them. The pair forms a V-shape that creates an open, lacy fabric without any complex construction. This is one of the quickest ways to make a blanket that reads as textured rather than plain.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 2 (Internet Archive). V-stitch and open-stitch variations in traditional British patterns.
heroPrompt: A swatch of V-stitch in cream DK cotton showing the open, airy fabric with clear V-shapes formed by treble pairs. Natural background.

glossaryTerms.definition: Two trebles worked into the same base stitch or chain space with one chain between them. The pair forms a V shape when viewed from the front. Creates an open, lacy fabric in a simple one-row repeat.

content.text: is (tr, ch 1, tr) all into the same stitch or chain space. The chain creates a small eyelet between the two treble legs, which catches the light and reads as lacy from any distance. The fabric is open and drapes well. A single-row repeat makes it one of the more straightforward ways to produce a lacy blanket.
Row 1 (setup): ch 4, tr in 5th ch from hook, *skip 2 ch, V-st (tr, ch 1, tr) in next ch; repeat from * across, tr in last ch (7 V-stitches). Turn.
Row 2: ch 4 (counts as tr + ch 1), tr into the ch-1 space of the first V-stitch, *V-st into the ch-1 space of each V-stitch across, tr at end. Turn.

attrs.title: Work into the chain space, not the chain itself
attrs.body: On return rows, the V-stitch goes into the ch-1 space (the gap under the chain), not through the chain link itself. Insert the hook under the whole chain, not into one of its loops. This is what gives the openwork character; working through the chain tightens the gap and loses the lacy effect.

content.text: V-stitch works cleanly in hexagons and other in-the-round motifs. Place one V-stitch at each increase point with ch 2 between the V-stitches for the increase. The ch-1 inside each V-stitch stays constant; the ch-2 between V-stitches at corners is the increase.

attrs.heading: V-stitch problems
attrs.intro: Two problems that come up with V-stitch.

items.symptom: The fabric tightens and the V-shapes disappear
items.cause: Working into the chain links rather than into the chain space.
items.fix: Insert the hook under the whole chain-1 bar, not through its loops. The chain should sit freely in the centre of each V.

items.symptom: The stitch count changes from row to row
items.cause: Working an extra stitch at the edge, or missing the last V-stitch at the end of the row.
items.fix: Mark the first V-stitch of each row and count the V-stitches at the end of row 1. That count must stay constant every row.

content.text: The fan stitch is a V-stitch expanded: instead of (tr, ch 1, tr), a fan is (tr, ch 1) three or four times plus a final tr, all into the same chain space. The granny cluster uses a similar principle with three-treble groups instead of single trebles.
